definitions.explanation: A child enrolled in a kindergarten or nursery school. Used in both casual and official contexts to refer to young children in pre-elementary education.

examples.japanese: {園児|えんじ}たちが{遊|あそ}んでいる。
{園児|えんじ}の{送|おく}り{迎|むか}えは{毎日|まいにち}{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: Dropping off and picking up the kindergartener every day is tough.

examples.japanese: この{幼稚園|ようちえん}では{園児|えんじ}が{自分|じぶん}で{弁当|べんとう}を{用意|ようい}する{日|ひ}がある。
examples.english: At this kindergarten, there are days when the children prepare their own lunch boxes.

notes:
USAGE:
Refers specifically to children enrolled in a {幼稚園|ようちえん} (kindergarten) or {保育園|ほいくえん} (nursery school). Not used for children who simply happen to be young — the word implies enrollment in a pre-school institution.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {園児|えんじ}{募集|ぼしゅう} (recruiting kindergarteners; enrollment call)
- {園児|えんじ}の{保護者|ほごしゃ} (guardians of kindergarten children)
- {園児|えんじ}{数|すう} (number of enrolled children)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {幼児|ようじ}: young child — broader term for any small child, regardless of school enrollment
- {児童|じどう}: school child — refers to elementary school-age children
